entities.name: Subsensory vibratory insole
observations: Piezoelectric shoe insoles delivered stochastic-resonance mechanical noise at 70% and 85% of each participant's sensory threshold in healthy adults aged 65–90 years.
Acute stimulation reduced postural-sway area, improved Timed Up and Go performance, and reduced temporal walking variability in a small randomized crossover study.

entities.name: Healthy older adults
observations: The direct evidence involved 12 healthy community-dwelling adults aged 65–90 years in a randomized, single-blind, 3-day crossover study.
A related analysis used the same 12 healthy elderly participants and found significant reductions in all eight measured quiet-standing sway parameters with subsensory foot noise.

entities.name: PMID:25450133
observations: Small randomized, single-blind, 3-day crossover study in 12 healthy adults aged 65–90 years; subsensory stochastic-resonance insoles improved Timed Up and Go, reduced postural-sway area, and reduced temporal walking variability during testing.
Sensory thresholds were relatively stable within and across days, but persistent post-removal benefit and fall prevention were not established.

entities.name: PMID:16287079
observations: In a related analysis including 12 healthy elderly participants, subsensory foot noise significantly reduced all eight measured quiet-standing sway parameters versus no noise.
The analysis did not provide elderly-specific gait outcomes, effect sizes, or long-term follow-up.

entities.name: Acute balance gait benefit
observations: In selected healthy older adults, subsensory vibratory insoles probably improve acute standing balance and selected mobility/gait measures, but evidence is based mainly on one small crossover trial and a related analysis.
No convincing evidence establishes sustained gait improvement, reduced falls, or benefit after removing the insoles.
